design.estimator: offset = n/(n+kappa) * mean(y - y_hat | calibration rows of the test paper)
design.kappa_definition: sigma2_noise / tau2_paper, both method-of-moments on training folds
design.oracle_bound: per-paper mean residual removed with no sampling and no shrinkage, scored on the n_cal=0 row set: the ceiling for any estimator that only shifts a paper by a constant

oracle_bound.definition: subtract each test paper's own mean residual over all its rows; same evaluation rows as n_cal=0; no sampling, no kappa

kill.rule: R^2 at n_cal=10 < 0.40 closes the per-paper calibration line

round5.purpose: sampling floor behind the n_cal=10 headline

kill.rule: 5th percentile at n_cal=10 < 0.45 means 0.6839 may only be quoted as a mean, never as a deployment guarantee

caveats: The calibration rows are drawn from the same paper as the evaluation rows. That is the deployment regime being modelled, not a leak: the correction uses their labels, and those rows are then excluded from scoring.
kappa is estimated on the training folds of each outer split, so a test paper's own residual scale never enters its shrinkage factor.
The affine arm has two free parameters from n_cal rows; at n_cal<=2 it degenerates to the offset arm and is reported for the decomposition only.
James-Stein borrows strength across the other held-out papers in the same fold, which is a batch-arrival assumption no single-paper deployment satisfies.
Papers with one row cannot be both calibrated and evaluated, so they leave the n_cal>0 row sets entirely; n_eval_rows records how much of the cohort is lost.

The oracle bound is not deployable: it removes each test paper's mean residual using every one of that paper's evaluation rows. It is the ceiling for any estimator that only shifts a paper by a constant, quoted to bound the curve.
